_what: npm cmd shims, generated by npm's own generator -- not written by hand.
_how: node -e "import cmdShim from '<npm>/node_modules/cmd-shim/lib/index.js'; await cmdShim(<target>, <bin>)" against npm 11's bundled cmd-shim, macOS, 2026-09-11. A .cmd shim is the shape every npm install of `claude`/`copilot` produces on Windows, and it is what `shutil.which` resolves there.
_why: tests/test_windows_launch.py parses these on whatever OS the suite is running on. Recording the generator's real output means the parser is tested against the artifact rather than against somebody's memory of it.

claude.cmd.note: the ordinary case: a `node` shebang with no flags. The doubled space before the quoted target is the generator's own (`"%_prog%" ${args} ${target}` with an empty `args`).

copilot.cmd.note: npm copies the target's shebang flags into the shim, so the launcher has to carry them too -- starting the program without them would be starting it differently from the way its own installer does.

compiled-tool.cmd.note: no shebang, so npm writes a shim that runs the target directly and there is no JavaScript entry point to find. The fallback case: launch the shim as a batch file and say so in the launch log.
